en.title: Minimum Suffix Flips Starting from an All-Zero String
en.description:
Start with an all-0 string of the same length. Each step picks one position and toggles 0/1 at that position and every position to its right. Find the minimum number of steps to obtain the target.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains the length n, and the second line contains the binary target string; an empty string is written as an empty line. Original bounds: Unknown. This site uses 0≤n≤200000; the catalog's 100,000 bound is not original evidence.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; 0; 1. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Scan from left to right while maintaining the current effective bit; whenever it differs from the target, flip the suffix once and update the effective bit.
